insurer: Aditya Birla Health Insurance Co. Limited
sumInsured: ₹50 Lakhs to ₹6 Crores (as per Product Benefit Table)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: Room Rent ... Actuals up to Sum Insured
great.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (VIP+), Hospitalization Treatment (In-built Cover)
great.explanation: Room rent is payable at actuals up to the Sum Insured with no room-category cap mentioned. This reduces the risk of room-rent based deductions and gives you flexibility to choose a room within your Sum Insured.

great.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
great.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred... for up to 90 days immediately prior to the date of such Hospitalization.
great.explanation: Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 90 days before admission. This helps pay for consultations, tests, and medicines leading up to hospitalization.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: We shall provide for a reload amounting to the Base Sum Insured (“Super Reload”), unlimited times during the Policy Year...
great.explanation: A reload equal to the Base Sum Insured is available unlimited times in the same policy year. This can significantly increase available cover if you have multiple hospitalizations in one year.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: an additional limit under the current Policy Year (“Super Credit”) will be applied / increased... irrespective of any claims in previous Policy Year
great.explanation: An additional limit (“Super Credit”) is applied/increased for the current policy year irrespective of claims in the previous year. This means your available coverage can grow even if you made claims earlier.

great.name: Bariatric Surgery
great.quote: Obesity Treatment: Medical Expenses incurred... for a Bariatric Surgery... subject to the conditions that needs to be fulfilled as per Section D.1.6
great.explanation: Medical expenses for bariatric surgery are covered, subject to the conditions in Section D.1.6. This can reduce out-of-pocket costs for medically indicated obesity treatment.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries / treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage...
good.reference: Section D.1.2 Specified disease / procedure Waiting Period (Code-Excl02)
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are not covered until 24 months of continuous coverage are completed. Claims for those listed conditions will be payable only after you finish this 2-year wait.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are excluded for the first 30 days from the policy start date, except accidents. This is a standard waiting period you should plan around when buying a new policy.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote:
Pre Existing Disease (PED) Waiting Period
3 years
good.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (VIP+), Waiting Period - Inbuilt Cover
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after a waiting period of 3 years. You cannot claim for declared/known pre-existing conditions until this period is completed.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: The Company shall indemnify the Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses incurred... for up to 180 days from the date of discharge from the Hospital.
good.explanation: Post-hospitalization medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge. This is market-standard support for follow-up tests, medicines, and consultations after hospitalization.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-Payment: means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the Policyholder / Insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
bad.explanation: Only a definition of co-payment is provided here and no applied co-pay clause is shown in the quoted text. If the schedule/benefit table does not impose any co-pay, you would not have to share a percentage of admissible claims.

unclear.name: Consumables
unclear.quote: The expenses that are not covered... may be covered under this Product if Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver) is applicable to You and mentioned in the Policy Schedule.
unclear.reference: Annexure Summary; also Section C.4 / Annexure I context
unclear.explanation: Non-medical/consumable items are covered only if the optional 'Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver)' is applicable and shown in the Policy Schedule. If it is not included for you, these items may be out-of-pocket during hospitalization.

unclear.name: Consumables
unclear.quote: Claim Protect (Non-Medical Expense Waiver): Non-payable items will be covered (all 4 lists of Annexure I)
unclear.reference: Annexure III - Product Benefit Table (VIP+); also Section C.4
unclear.explanation: The benefit table states non-payable items (all 4 lists in Annexure I) will be covered under 'Claim Protect'. Whether you get this depends on whether Claim Protect is included for you in the Policy Schedule.
